skim: A Himalayan glacier collapse violent enough to register as a 5.2-magnitude earthquake unleashed the Nepal-Tibet flash flood, whose toll has now climbed past 540 dead with over 2,000 still missing.
New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish first Jackson Hole speech reversed gold's rally, knocked bitcoin down 3.3% to $77,678, and pushed September rate-hike odds toward 50-50.
Nvidia's blowout Q2 (revenue up 106% to $96.2 billion) drew a rival jab from OpenAI's new in-house Jalapeño chip, unveiled the same week as a warning shot at Nvidia's margins.

PM Modi opened a four-day Central Asia trip in Tashkent ahead of the SCO summit in Bishkek, where a brief Modi-Xi meeting is expected before Xi's full state visit to Delhi for the Sept 12-13 BRICS summit.

Iran named its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz as Qatar's PM joined Pakistan and Oman as a third mediator, while England tightened its grip on the Lord's Test and India's Women's T20 Asia Cup bid opened in Dubai.

stories.headline: Nepal-Tibet Flood Toll Passes 540, Over 2,000 Still Missing
stories.body: A Himalayan glacier collapse that unleashed catastrophic flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border on Aug 26 — a surge powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event — has now killed at least 543 people, with more than 2,000 still missing across both countries, including 90 Americans and hundreds of foreign trekkers, per ABC News (Aug 28). “They were like excited for this trip. It was like a spiritual, religious like trek they’d been looking forward to,” said Siddarth Venkatachalam, whose mother is among the missing.

stories.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Now the Deadliest On Record
stories.body: WHO data through Aug 26 confirms the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the largest ever recorded, with 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths — a 48.1% case-fatality ratio — spread across 60 health zones in six provinces, per The Watchers (Aug 29). Only 1,293 patients have recovered so far as treatment centres race to contain the spread.

stories.headline: Philippine Storms Kill 32, Displace Millions as Leptospirosis Tops 5,000 Cases
stories.body: The Philippines’ Office of Civil Defense says tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng combined with the seasonal habagat monsoon have killed 32 people and affected roughly 8 million people across 2.3 million families, with 117 local governments under a state of calamity, per Philstar (Aug 29). The flooding has fuelled a nationwide leptospirosis outbreak that reached 5,486 cases as of Aug 26; DOH Secretary Edwin Mercado said “we expect cases to increase in the next two weeks following the rains and flooding,” per Manila Bulletin (Aug 28).

stories.headline: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope Set for Sunday Launch
stories.body: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy carrying NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope rolled out to Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39A ahead of a targeted 7:26am EDT liftoff on Aug 30, per NASA (Aug 29). The school-bus-sized observatory will travel over a million miles from Earth to, in the words of NASA’s Shawn Domagal-Goldman, help astronomers “explore dark matter, dark energy, exoplanets, and almost anything from our own solar system to galaxies at the edge of the observable universe.”

stories.headline: India Close Out Sri Lanka Series 1–0 After Colombo Stalemate
stories.body: Sri Lanka salvaged an “epic draw” in the second Test at Colombo as Sonal Dinusha’s twin centuries (103 and an unbeaten 133) denied India a series sweep, per Gulf News (Aug 27). India, built on Devdutt Padikkal’s 328 series runs, had declared at 503-9 but could not bowl out Sri Lanka a second time as the hosts closed on 429-9; captain Shubman Gill still called it a job well done, saying “Test cricket won today.” India take the two-match series 1-0.

stories.headline: England Tighten Grip on Lord’s Test as Pakistan Reel
stories.body: Babar Azam’s comeback has done little to arrest Pakistan’s slide at Lord’s, where England built a 261-run lead by the close of a rain-hit day three, per The Express Tribune (Aug 29). Pakistan were skittled for 110 in their first innings — Ollie Robinson taking 4-11 and Jofra Archer three — before England’s reply, anchored by Emilio Gay, weathered further weather delays. Pakistan already trail 1-0 in the three-match series, leaving little margin left to level it.

stories.headline: Harmanpreet’s India Open Asia Cup Title Bid Against Thailand
stories.body: The Women’s T20 Asia Cup is underway in Dubai, with India — the competition’s most successful side historically — opening their campaign against Thailand on Aug 30 under fresh scrutiny after nine defeats in 16 T20Is this year and a group-stage World Cup exit, per Rozana Spokesman (Aug 29). Middle-order worries have deepened with Jemimah Rodrigues ruled out, bringing Pratika Rawal into the squad as cover. The tournament runs through Sept 13 and builds toward the blockbuster India-Pakistan meeting on Sept 5.

stories.headline: Arsenal Draw Real Madrid, Barcelona Face PSG in Champions League Draw
stories.body: Thursday’s 36-team Champions League league-phase draw in Monaco threw up heavyweight fixtures for 2026-27: Arsenal host Real Madrid but travel to Bayern Munich, while Barcelona face both PSG and Manchester City at home, per NBC Sports/Yahoo Sports (Aug 27). Liverpool were paired at home with Atletico Madrid, and City must also make the trip to Paris to face PSG. The league phase runs into January, building toward the final at Atletico Madrid’s Estadio Metropolitano on June 5, 2027.

stories.headline: Norris Cuts Into Antonelli’s Lead With Zandvoort Double
stories.body: Lando Norris’s back-to-back Zandvoort wins trimmed his title deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points with 11 races left, per Sky Sports (Aug 24). McLaren boss Andrea Stella credited a Budapest upgrade package, saying Norris is “driving and operating at a very high level,” though the Briton stayed cautious: “I need more than what I have now,” he said. Attention now turns to Monza, where Antonelli is set to carry a grid penalty into the Italian Grand Prix.

stories.headline: Fed Chief Warsh Turns Hawkish at Jackson Hole
stories.body: In his first Jackson Hole address as Fed chair, Kevin Warsh warned that recent inflation reports “do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved,” and said the Fed “may have to raise interest rates in the coming months” unless price growth moves toward target “clearly and at sufficient speed,” per PBS NewsHour (Aug 28). The hawkish tone pushed the two-year Treasury yield from 4.22% to 4.30% and lifted market-implied odds of a September rate hike from roughly a third to near 50-50, rattling gold, bitcoin and equities.

stories.headline: Gold Slides 3% as Dollar Rallies on Warsh’s Hawkish Turn
stories.body: Gold retreated roughly 3% after Warsh’s speech as the dollar rebounded and September rate-hike odds jumped to 57.5% from 35.4% a day earlier, per XTB (Aug 28). “Assets that tend to be negatively correlated with the dollar are pulling back today, including EURUSD, gold, Bitcoin and even Wall Street equities,” XTB analysts wrote, pausing the metal’s multi-week climb that had carried it above $4,700/oz on Fed bond-buyback optimism.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Tumbles From 3-Month High After Warsh Remarks
stories.body: Bitcoin fell 3.3% to $77,678, erasing most of Thursday’s run to a three-month high near $81,330, after Warsh’s hawkish remarks pushed September rate-hike odds on Polymarket to 68%, per Eastern Herald (Aug 29). “Higher expected rates strengthen the dollar and lift real yields, reducing demand for non-yielding assets including Bitcoin,” the outlet noted, adding that a $6.4 billion options expiry at CME that morning amplified the selloff by removing hedging buffers.

stories.headline: Crude Holds Near 2026 Highs Despite Dollar Swings
stories.body: WTI crude traded at $83.40 a barrel on Aug 29, per ConvexTrade, with Brent near $90.55 a day earlier per Fortune (Aug 28), both holding close to the year’s highs even as the dollar firmed on Warsh’s hawkish tilt. Prices remain supported after OPEC+ completed its rollback of 1.65 million barrels per day in voluntary output cuts with a further September hike, removing a supply overhang that had weighed on the market.

stories.headline: Wall Street Hits Records Ahead of Fed Speech
stories.body: The Dow closed at 53,569.44 (+0.2%), the S&P 500 at 7,730.99 (+0.7%) and the Nasdaq at 26,541.35 (+1.6%) on Thursday, led by a tech-earnings rally after strong results from several large names, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28). The records came just ahead of Warsh’s Jackson Hole address, which investors were watching closely for clarity on the Fed’s rate path.

stories.headline: Nvidia’s Blowout Quarter Silences Bubble Skeptics — For Now
stories.body: Nvidia posted Q2 revenue of $96.2 billion (up 106% year-over-year) and data-center revenue of $89 billion, then guided to roughly 70% sales growth through fiscal 2028, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28). “AI has reached its inflection point. It’s doing useful work,” CEO Jensen Huang said, though supply-chain commitments doubled to $279 billion, underscoring that capacity — not demand — is now the bottleneck.

stories.headline: OpenAI’s New Jalapeño Chip Fires a Warning Shot at Nvidia
stories.body: OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip, claiming 1.5-1.9x more AI work per watt and up to 4.1x better performance on interactive workloads than Nvidia’s GB200/GB300 while drawing far less power (550W vs. 1,200-1,400W), per 24/7 Wall St. (Aug 26). OpenAI added it “will continue to widely deploy accelerators from NVIDIA and other partners for both training and inference workloads,” but analysts said the disclosure itself signals rising competitive pressure on Nvidia’s margins from custom silicon.

stories.headline: Meta Preps ‘Hatch’ AI Agents and $199.99 Premium Tier
stories.body: Meta is finalizing its consumer AI agent platform, Hatch, for launch as soon as late August or early September, built on its OpenClaw technology and integrating with DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Microsoft Outlook, per Forkast News via Yahoo Finance (Aug 25). A premium subscription could run up to $199.99 a month, while a new flagship model, “Watermelon,” targeting GPT-5.5-level performance on internal benchmarks, is slated for October as part of Mark Zuckerberg’s push to monetize AI beyond advertising.

stories.headline: Anthropic Weighs Letting Early Shareholders Cash Out in IPO
stories.body: Anthropic plans to unveil its IPO prospectus after Labor Day with a potential listing in late September or early October, per The Information (via The Daily Guardian, Aug 27), and is now considering letting some existing shareholders sell stock in the offering, The Information’s Jessica Lessin said on CNBC’s Squawk Box (Aug 28). The filing follows reports the company is targeting a valuation north of $2 trillion — which would make it the largest IPO on record, eclipsing SpaceX’s $1.77 trillion June debut.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Presses Microsoft, Amazon, Google for Kimi K3 Cut
stories.body: China’s Moonshot AI is negotiating for up to a 30% revenue share from Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS and Google Cloud on services built atop its 2.8-trillion-parameter, 1-million-token-context Kimi K3 model, per TradingKey (Aug 26). “Moonshot AI is seeking up to a 30% cut of the revenue generated from K3-related services on the three major cloud platforms,” the report said, noting talks remain early-stage with revenue mechanisms, data access and token audits still unresolved — the news comes after Moonshot raised a $3.5 billion Series F at a $35 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Ukraine Strikes Force Shutdown of Russia’s Fourth-Largest Refinery
stories.body: A Ukrainian drone strike on Aug 26 forced Russia’s NORSI refinery in Nizhny Novgorod — the country’s fourth-largest and second-biggest gasoline producer — to halt crude processing for the fifth time in five months, per Euromaidan Press (Aug 27). With Lukoil’s Perm and Volgograd plants also down, Russia has reinstated gasoline rationing in Moscow and St Petersburg and extended its diesel export ban, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov promised a “harsh response.”

stories.headline: Iran Sets Terms for Reopening Hormuz as Qatar Joins Mediation
stories.body: Iran says it will formally lay out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz — including a lifted port blockade, war-damage compensation and sanctions relief — after Qatar’s prime minister became the third mediator, following Pakistan and Oman, to visit Tehran in a week, per Al Jazeera (Aug 28). “The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran’s conditions, and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz,” said Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, while Trump said “I have no time schedule, none. I’m not in a hurry.”

stories.headline: Mossad Chief, Syrian FM Meet Again in Jordan Over Turkey Tensions
stories.body: Mossad chief Roman Gofman met Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani in Jordan for further US-mediated talks aimed at defusing tensions that flared after Israel bombed Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase on Aug 18, claiming it was being readied for Turkish forces, per Turkish Minute (Aug 26). Damascus is pushing for an Israeli withdrawal to pre-Assad positions and a restored 1974 buffer-zone deal, while Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israeli forces would stay on Mount Hermon, citing what he called jihadist threats.

stories.headline: Xi-Trump Summit Set for Sept 24, Trade Truce Extension “Almost Certain”
stories.body: Xi Jinping is expected to meet Donald Trump in Washington on Sep 24, with the year-long trade truce reached in Busan last October likely to be extended, per South China Morning Post (Aug 28). Chinese and US officials are still deciding whether business leaders will join Xi’s delegation to reciprocate Trump’s May visit to Beijing; US Ambassador David Perdue called that trip “very successful” and said Washington is preparing for “important high-level interactions.”

fixtures.headline: India vs Pakistan, Women's T20 Asia Cup
fixtures.body: The tournament's marquee clash lands in Dubai with both Group A rivals looking to book a semi-final spot ahead of the Sept 13 final.

fixtures.headline: Champions League Matchday One
fixtures.body: The revamped 36-team league phase kicks off across two days, with Arsenal, Barcelona, Liverpool and Manchester City all in action in fixtures set by last week's draw.

fixtures.headline: Italian Grand Prix at Monza
fixtures.body: Lando Norris chases further gains on points leader Kimi Antonelli at F1's fastest circuit, where Antonelli is expected to start from the back after a grid penalty.

portfolio.headline: PayPal’s Buyout Talks With Stripe and Advent Collapse
portfolio.body: Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International have abandoned their reported $50 billion approach to acquire PayPal, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 28), ending weeks of takeover speculation that had been propping up the stock. Analyst Josh Kohn-Lindquist argued PayPal “still trades at only 7.5 times free cash flow,” suggesting underlying value remains even without a deal. No new operating issue was cited — the move reflects the loss of acquisition-premium speculation rather than any change to PayPal’s business.

portfolio.headline: Nvidia Beats on Revenue but Guides to Thinner Margins
portfolio.body: Nvidia posted fiscal second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion, more than doubling year-over-year and beating Wall Street’s $92.2 billion estimate, with data-center revenue up 117% to $89 billion, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 27). CFO Colette Kress guided gross margins down toward 71–72% by fiscal Q4 from the current 75%, saying “memory scarcity today is being driven in large part by the AI buildout itself.” Forward supply commitments more than doubled to $279 billion, underscoring how much capacity Nvidia has locked in to meet AI demand.

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Notches a Record Quarter, Then Gives Some Back
portfolio.body: CrowdStrike reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $1.47 billion, up 26% year-over-year and above the $1.44 billion consensus, with net-new annual recurring revenue of $332.8 million marking a company record, per Vantage Markets (Aug 28). The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $5.99–$6.01 billion, with CEO George Kurtz crediting demand for the Falcon Flex platform, though a newly disclosed $13.1 million legal accrual tied to last year’s July outage drew attention, per TradingKey (Aug 28).

portfolio.headline: Amazon Leans Further Into AI Infrastructure and Clean Power
portfolio.body: Amazon signed new renewable-energy power purchase agreements in Europe, including offshore wind commitments in Germany and wind-farm deals in Sweden, to support its expanding AWS and AI data-center footprint, per TradingKey (Aug 28). Analysts reiterated buy ratings and lifted price targets to an average near $320, citing “accelerating enterprise demand for cloud migration, higher adoption of custom data center processors alongside expanded GPU integrations, and robust underlying retail fundamentals,” though some investors flagged Amazon’s roughly $220 billion 2026 capital-expenditure plan as a capital-efficiency question.

portfolio.headline: Figma Posts a Third Straight Quarter of Accelerating Growth
portfolio.body: Figma reported second-quarter revenue of $370.1 million, up 48% year-over-year, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $40 million to $1.463–$1.467 billion, per StockTitan (Aug 11). CEO Dylan Field called it “Figma’s third straight quarter of accelerated revenue growth,” pointing to AI credit monetization and a new Figma agent that more than half of its largest customers now use weekly. Net dollar retention held at 136%, with customers paying $10,000-plus in annual recurring revenue up 34% year-over-year to nearly 16,000.

portfolio.headline: Rackspace Cuts Its Outlook as It Pivots Toward AI Compute
portfolio.body: Rackspace Technology lowered its full-year revenue guidance to $2.45–$2.55 billion, roughly a 7% cut at the midpoint, as it exits lower-margin public-cloud resale business in favor of AI compute, per Yahoo Finance (Aug 11). The company detailed new AI partnerships, including with Palantir, and said it expects $15–$20 million of revenue per megawatt of deployed AI compute capacity, though margin benefits aren’t expected until 2027. It also announced a $250 million at-the-market equity offering to fund the GPU buildout, adding near-term dilution on top of the guidance cut.

portfolio.headline: Arm Holdings Cools Off After a Multi-Week AI Rally
portfolio.body: Arm Holdings pulled back after a strong multi-day advance driven by positive semiconductor earnings and an expanded partnership with IBM on enterprise workloads, per TradingKey (Aug 28). With shares trading near 100 times forward earnings, the report characterized the pullback as valuation-driven consolidation rather than a reaction to fresh company news, compounded by routine executive share sales disclosed in SEC filings. Arm’s longer-term case — adoption of its v9 architecture and custom AI CPU designs among cloud hyperscalers — was described as intact.

portfolio.headline: Coeur Mining Slides With No Clear Catalyst Behind It
portfolio.body: No company-specific announcement accompanied Coeur Mining’s decline, per GuruFocus (Aug 28); the piece instead flagged valuation concerns and noted that insiders had sold about $5.6 million of stock over the prior year, calling that pattern a potential “red flag.” Coeur is a small-cap silver and gold miner with high sensitivity to metals prices and broader risk sentiment, and no company-specific news was found to explain the session’s move.

stories.headline: Modi Lands in Tashkent, Sets Up Xi Meeting at SCO Summit
stories.body: PM Modi arrived in Uzbekistan Aug 29 to begin a four-day Central Asia trip, greeted personally by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev — his fourth visit since 2015. “Landed in Tashkent to a warm welcome by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Grateful to him for the special gesture,” Modi posted, per Organiser (Aug 29). He heads next to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan for the 26th SCO Summit (Aug 31–Sept 1), where a brief bilateral with Xi Jinping is expected ahead of Xi’s full state visit to Delhi for the Sept 12–13 BRICS summit.

stories.headline: Ex-CDS Chauhan: Modi Gave Forces ‘Complete Freedom’ Before Sindoor
stories.body: Former Chief of Defence Staff Gen Anil Chauhan detailed PM Modi’s April 29 directive ahead of Operation Sindoor, per WION (Aug 26): “The Prime Minister told us only one thing: that he is not under any kind of political pressure to do it immediately,” with orders to leave “no reason for failure, either human or because of technical reasons.” Chauhan said India’s escalation doctrine ensured “the winning note will always be delivered by us and not by the Pakistanis” during the operation, launched May 7 and paused May 10 after Pakistan sought a ceasefire.

stories.headline: US Sanctions Four India-Based Firms Over $119mn Iran Oil Trade
stories.body: Washington sanctioned four India-based companies and three individuals for allegedly moving $119 million in Iranian petroleum products, per Business Today (Aug 26). Sadashiva Overseas Limited was flagged for roughly $69 million in imports between February 2024 and June 2025, alongside PP Softtech, Prakrutees Infra Impex and customs broker Portease Partners; nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels — including about 20 China/Hong Kong-based firms — were hit in the same action. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called it part of an effort to “tighten the noose” on Iran, describing it as an “economic D-Day.”

stories.headline: Burnham Eyes September US Trip to Press Trump on Ukraine
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham said he is “looking forward to going to New York” next month for the UN General Assembly to lobby President Trump for more Patriot missiles for Ukraine, per ITV News (Aug 25). Speaking after visiting Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th independence anniversary, Burnham noted “there are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with” and pledged the UK would share Scalp missile production blueprints, as European allies scramble to plug gaps left by Middle East conflicts diverting US air-defence stock.

stories.headline: UK Inflation Expectations Jump to 3.9%, Complicating BoE Path
stories.body: A Citi/YouGov survey found British households' 12-month inflation expectations jumped to 3.9% in August from 3.4% in July, with longer-term expectations rising to 4.1% — the highest since April — per Yahoo Finance/Reuters (Aug 25). Citi called the reversal “hawkish,” warning that energy prices tied to the Iran conflict could feed sustained price pressure, though it cautioned against reading too much into a single report as the Bank of England weighs its next move.

stories.headline: Reform UK Sinks to 18-Month Polling Low Amid Infighting
stories.body: Reform UK has fallen to 23% in the latest More in Common poll, its lowest level in over 18 months, level with a resurgent Labour on 27% and the Conservatives on 22%, per Left Foot Forward (Aug 26). The slide follows Nigel Farage's undeclared £5 million crypto-donor gift now facing a Standards Committee review, candidates' far-right remarks, and local-government infighting — support has fallen from roughly 30% a year ago into the low twenties now.

stories.headline: Qatar Condemns Israeli Storming of UNRWA Training Center
stories.body: Qatar's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned Israeli occupation forces for entering the Qalandiya Training Center run by UNRWA in occupied East Jerusalem, calling it “a blatant violation of international humanitarian law,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 26). Doha warned the move appears aimed at dismantling UNRWA and cutting services to millions of Palestinians across Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, and urged the international community to take “immediate protective measures” for UNRWA facilities.

stories.headline: Qatar Hosts Iran for Hormuz De-Escalation Talks
stories.body: Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Iranian officials to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz, floating a temporary shipping corridor and a possible “joint project” to clear the strait of mines, per Al Jazeera (Aug 27). Tehran, which has controlled the waterway since the February 28 war began, is demanding Washington lift its naval blockade and oil sanctions before reopening it; Qatar and Pakistan are mediating alongside Oman, with no deal yet reached.

stories.headline: GCC Agrees Joint Cybersecurity Framework Amid Regional Tensions
stories.body: Qatar's NCSA chief Eng. Abdulrahman bin Ali Al Farahid Al Malki joined the fifth GCC Ministerial Committee for Cybersecurity in Manama, which formally adopted joint frameworks to harmonize Gulf defence protocols, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 28). Ministers authorized the sixth and seventh Gulf Cyber Drills to test resilience against multi-vector attacks, with officials saying “safeguarding the Gulf's interconnected digital economy requires synchronised regional action rather than isolated defence models” as regional tensions escalate.

doha_events.headline: Doha Trade Fair
doha_events.body: A wide-ranging shopping fair with retailers spanning multiple product categories, running Aug 24–Sept 4 at the Doha Exhibition & Convention Center; free entry.

doha_events.headline: Discover the World Behind Kalila wa Dimna
doha_events.body: A long-running exhibition at the Museum of Islamic Art Library exploring the classic fable collection through manuscript replicas and architectural models, on view Aug 25–Dec 30; free entry.

doha_events.headline: Rouda Al Malki Exhibition
doha_events.body: A curated pop-up of women's fashion and lifestyle essentials at the Qatar National Convention Center, Aug 28–Sept 2; free entry.

doha_events.headline: ORBIT Arabian Night ft. Cheba Souad
doha_events.body: A live Rai music performance by Algerian singer Cheba Souad at Cielo Hotel, Lusail, on Aug 28; 21+, tickets from QAR 100 via Q-Tickets.

doha_events.headline: Travancore Fest: Mentalist Anandhu — The Secret Letter
doha_events.body: An interactive mentalism and storytelling show at Regency Hall on Aug 28, blending illusion with audience participation; tickets from QAR 100.
